 TSH Resources seeks independent assessment over Indonesia fires, haze
 TheStar 
 Mon, Nov 02, 2026 09:44am - 47 minutes 
 View Original 
 KUALA LUMPUR: TSH Resources Bhd has offered to voluntarily engage independent assessors at its own expense to examine its operations, corporate relationships and supply chains in connection with fires in Indonesia that have contributed to transboundary haze.
 In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the plantation group said it had written to Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) confirming its willingness to engage assessors from the Singapore government's panel.
 The move follows notices issued by NEA to its Singapore-incorporated subsidiaries, TSH Oversea Pte Ltd and TSH Global Plantation Pte Ltd, under Section 10(1) of Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014.
 “The company will cooperate with the assessors in carrying out their assessment, in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements, and as may be directed by NEA,” it said. 
 ...
 Summary Overview 
 • TSH Resources Bhd has voluntarily offered to fund independent assessors from Singapore's government panel to examine its operations, corporate relationships, and supply chains linked to Indonesian fires and transboundary haze.
• The initiative follows formal notices issued by Singapore's National Environment Agency to TSH's Singapore-incorporated subsidiaries, TSH Oversea Pte Ltd and TSH Global Plantation Pte Ltd, under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014.
• The plantation group confirmed its willingness to cooperate fully and transparently with the assessors and relevant authorities, aligning with Singapore's regulatory requirements and environmental concerns.
• TSH Resources stated it will continue to monitor the situation and make further announcements to Bursa Malaysia should any material developments arise from the assessment process.
